text: You are not your passing thoughts; you are the one who is aware of them.
source: A core idea of Advaita Vedanta — the witness (sākṣī)

text: Pleasure and pain come and go like seasons. Let them pass through.
Do your part with care, and loosen your grip on the result.
Evenness of mind is itself called yoga.
Be a friend to yourself; lift yourself up, gently.
Like a lamp in a still room, the settled mind does not flicker.
When the mind wanders, bring it back — kindly, as many times as it takes.
The mind is restless, yes. Practice and letting go steady it over time.
Like the ocean filled by rivers, stay deep and still while thoughts flow in.
Balance in food, rest, work and sleep is itself a quiet medicine for the heart.
Whole you began, and whole you remain.
One step from darkness toward light is enough for today.
Breath is the thread between body and mind; follow it home.
source: Teaching of prāṇāyāma in the yoga tradition

text: So — I breathe in. Ham — I breathe out. Rest in the simple rhythm.
source: So-Ham breath awareness, a traditional practice

text: Watch the clouds of thought; you are the sky they move through.
source: A common Vedantic image for awareness

text: The body is here, now. Feel your feet; you have arrived.
This moment is enough. You do not have to solve your whole life right now.
Arise, awake — and walk the path one patient step at a time.
